intro.p1: Ergo is a blockchain — a public ledger that anyone can read, nobody can edit, and no company runs. Its currency is called ERG.
intro.p2: If you've heard of Bitcoin, you already understand 70% of Ergo. Ergo keeps what Bitcoin does best — security through computing power (Proof-of-Work), money kept in locked boxes rather than accounts, and a fixed maximum number of coins — and adds something Bitcoin barely has: powerful yet safe smart contracts (rules attached to money that the network enforces by itself).

short.title: In one sentence
short.p1: Ergo is “programmable Bitcoin”: every coin on Ergo is kept inside a box, and every box carries a small set of rules saying who can open it and under what conditions.
short.p2: With Bitcoin, that rule is almost always “whoever can sign with this key may open it”. With Ergo, the rule can be “whoever can sign, and only after block 2,000,000, and only if at least 100 ERG is paid back to that other address”. Rules like these are what make decentralized exchanges, stablecoins, time-locked savings and more possible — without anyone holding your money for you.

pow.title: Proof-of-Work
pow.text: Secured by computing power like Bitcoin, not by how many coins you hold.

box.title: The box model (eUTXO)
box.text: Money lives in programmable, locked “boxes” instead of in accounts.

fair.title: Fair from the start
fair.text: No ICO, no pre-mine. Every ERG was created through mining.

fast.title: A block every ~2 minutes
fast.text: 5× faster than Bitcoin, while still safe for a decentralized network.

history.title: A little history
history.p1: Ergo's main network (mainnet) launched on 1 July 2019. It was built by a team of cryptography and blockchain researchers, including Alexander Chepurnoy and Dmitry Meshkov.
history.p2: Ergo launched without an ICO or any pre-sale of coins to investors. From the very first block, ERG could only be created one way: a miner finds a new block and collects the reward. During the first two years a small share of each reward (7.5 ERG per block) went to a development fund (the treasury), then tapered off and ended after about 2.5 years — and that was written into the network's rules from day one, where anyone could check it.

name.title: Where does the name “Ergo” come from?
name.p1: According to the <docs>official documentation</docs>, the name carries three layers of meaning:
name.latin: In Latin, ergo is a conjunction meaning “therefore” — as in “I think, therefore I am” — used to introduce a logical conclusion.
name.greek: In Greek, the related word ἔργον (ergon) means “work” — a subtle nod to the work of mining and maintaining the blockchain.
name.ticker: The ticker ERG also echoes the erg, a small unit of energy in physics — tying back to work and energy once more.

who.title: Who is Ergo for?
who.users: Everyday users who want to hold their own money and send and receive it quickly with very low fees (often just 0.001 ERG).
who.miners: GPU miners — the Autolykos v2 algorithm is designed so that specialized mining machines (ASICs) have a hard time dominating.
who.devs: Developers who want to write smart contracts whose behavior can be predicted before a transaction is sent.

trust.title: You don't need to trust us
trust.text: Every number on this page — block height, supply, hashrate — comes straight from the blockchain via explorer.erg.vn. That's the spirit of a blockchain: don't trust, verify.
